newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mayor Honorato Galvez of San Ildenfonso, Bulacan was acquitted of murder charges by the Quezon City regional trial court for the killing of Alvin Vinculado and the wounding of the latter's twin brother and uncle in 1993. The acquittal brought protests from the bereaved family and members of a group fighting for justice for victims of violence in the country (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Nine Mindanao legislators asked the Supreme Court to stop the government from implementing the Southern Philippine Council for Peace and Development (MALAYA)

- Local passenger car sales rose by 26.3 percent in the first three quarters of the year, a preliminary report from the Philippine Chamber of Automotive Manufacturing of the Philippines Inc said (INQUIRER).
- P.T. Gunung Garuda, one of Indonesia's largest steel-making firms, plan to put up a $150 million downstream steel venture in the Philippines (THE MANILA TIME)
- Manila stocks posted its second biggest drop for the year, with the main index down 83.49 points to 3,037.54 points, on foreign selling (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
-The International Monetary Fund has asked the Philippines to help out in IMF initiatives to help low income countries, Manila Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said. (MALAYA)

- Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co is losing at least one-billion pesos in revenues yearly from the illegal operations of fly-by-night telephone firms offering international services (MANILA BULLETIN)
